name: fsckclean
description:
THE CLEAN FLAG, BOTH WAYS.  2.11BSD update #456 puts MNT_CLEAN in the superblock's fs_flags when a filesystem is cleanly unmounted, and fsck(8) skips it unless -f.  That is what makes a boot fsck affordable: a full check of a 32000-block root reads the whole i-list and every block of every file through a single-block read path, measured at over 45 seconds.

BOTH ARMS ARE HERE BECAUSE EITHER ALONE IS VACUOUS.  `clean; not checking' on its own would pass for a fsck that refused the volume for some other reason and said so in a line nobody matched; `** Phase 1' on its own would pass for a build where the flag was never written.  Together they say the flag is read, honoured, and overridable.

/dev/rsd1 is the scratch spindle (disk/ufsscratch.po, via extra_hards), which fgxfs stamps clean as it writes -- a volume it has just finished writing is consistent by construction, which is the same statement a clean unmount makes.

screen_contains: file system is clean; not checking
